new.title: See the house where Atatürk stayed in Mersin
new.desc: The Mersin Atatürk House is a historic mansion in the old centre that hosted Mustafa Kemal Atatürk during his visit to the city in 1923 and is now a museum. It preserves period furniture and personal items in a typical late Ottoman Mersin house.
new.tip: Small museum, usually closed on Mondays; combine with the nearby old-town streets and Kent Müzesi.
new.q: Mersin Atatürk Evi, Cumhuriyet, Akdeniz, Mersin

new.title: Trace Cilicia at the Mersin Museum
new.desc: Mersin Museum holds finds from Yumuktepe, Soli, Elaiussa Sebaste and Uzuncaburç, from Neolithic pottery to Roman sculpture and Byzantine mosaics. It is the best single introduction to the archaeology of the province.
new.tip: Allow about 90 minutes; closed Mondays. Visit it before heading out to the ruins along the coast.
new.q: Mersin Müzesi, Mersin Arkeoloji Müzesi, Yenişehir, Mersin

new.title: Learn Mersin's port story at Mustafa Erim Kent Müzesi
new.desc: The Mustafa Erim Urban History Museum tells how a small fishing village grew into a major Mediterranean port in the 19th-century cotton and trade boom. It sits in an old building in the Akdeniz district, next to the historic centre.
new.tip: Small and quick, 30-45 minutes; a good rainy-day stop near the old market streets.
new.q: Mustafa Erim Mersin Kent Tarihi Müzesi, 5219 Sokak, Akdeniz, Mersin

new.title: Walk the 8,000-year-old layers of Yumuktepe
new.desc: Yumuktepe is a mound in the middle of the city with about 23 settlement layers going back to roughly 7000 BC, making it one of the oldest continuously inhabited sites in Anatolia. Excavated since the 1930s, it has a Neolithic village, Bronze Age fortifications and a Hittite-period wall.
new.tip: Open daily with a small entry fee; visit in the morning or late afternoon, there is little shade.

new.title: Walk the colonnade of Soli Pompeiopolis
new.desc: Soli was a Cilician port that Pompey resettled around 67 BC and renamed Pompeiopolis after defeating the pirates. Its main avenue still has a line of Corinthian columns running toward the silted harbour, with a Roman theatre and mole nearby.
new.tip: Free to wander; best at sunset, and the Viranşehir seafront fish places are a short walk away.
new.q: Soli Pompeiopolis Antik Kenti, Viranşehir, Mezitli, Mersin

new.title: Hike up to Gözne Castle above Mersin
new.desc: Gözne is a mountain village in the Toros foothills above Mersin with the ruins of a medieval castle and a cool-air yayla culture that Mersin families use as an escape from summer heat. The road passes citrus groves and pine forest.
new.tip: Go on a weekday in summer; the village restaurants serve trout and mountain food.

new.title: Eat levrek by the water at İskele Marin
new.desc: İskele Marin is a fish restaurant inside Mersin Marina, known for grilled sea bass and cold meze plates, with tables looking toward the yachts. It is one of the places locals take guests for a sea-view dinner.
new.tip: Book for weekend evenings; order the levrek and ask for the day's meze selection.
new.q: İskele Marin Restaurant, Adnan Menderes Bulvarı No:182, Eğriçam, Yenişehir, Mersin

new.title: Eat Mersin tantuni at Borsa Tantuni
new.desc: Tantuni is Mersin's signature street food: finely chopped beef sautéed in oil and wrapped in thin lavash with tomato, parsley and sumac. Borsa Tantuni in Yenişehir is known for tender beef fillet in tandır lavash.
new.tip: Order it with ayran and ask for acı (hot) on the side; best at lunch.

new.title: Eat kerebiç at Kerebiççi Hayri Usta
new.desc: Kerebiç is a Mersin and Tarsus speciality of layered semolina dough with pistachio and cinnamon, traditionally made for Ramadan. Hayri Usta in Kiremithane serves it with thick çöven cream and is one of the best-known makers.
new.tip: Eat it fresh with the cream on the side; it peaks in Ramadan.
new.q: Kerebiççi Hayri Usta, Kiremithane, İstiklal Cd., Akdeniz, Mersin

new.title: Buy cezerye at Dondurmacı Halil
new.desc: Cezerye is the carrot-and-coconut sweet of Mersin, cooked with sugar and nuts and sold in cut squares. Dondurmacı Halil is a local ice-cream institution that also sells cezerye, kerebiç and pumpkin dessert.
new.tip: Buy a box to take home; try the lemon ice cream while you are there.

new.title: Drink an atom at Atomcu Hamit
new.desc: Atom is a Mersin drink of milk with banana, avocado, forest fruit and nuts, served as a thick glass and eaten with a spoon. Atomcu Hamit is among the best-known places to try it.
new.tip: Share a large size; it is filling and works as dessert.

new.title: Eat ciğer on open bread at Ciğerci Saboş
new.desc: Mersin's ciğer culture revolves around skewered liver grilled over charcoal and served on flatbread with onion, sumac and chilli. Ciğerci Saboş in Kiremithane is one of the city's classic liver shops.
new.tip: Go at lunch when it is freshest; order ayran or şalgam with it.
new.q: Ciğerci Saboş, Kiremithane, Cemalettin Tanrıöver Sk., Akdeniz, Mersin

new.title: Eat lamb chops at Pirzolacı Fırat Usta
new.desc: Pirzolacı Fırat Usta in Toroslar grills lamb pirzola and kaburga on skewers, served with Silifke strained yogurt and pide. It is a local grill-house favourite.
new.tip: Order the mixed grill for two with the yogurt; evenings are busy.
new.q: Pirzolacı Fırat Usta, Karaisalı Caddesi No:107, Toroslar, Mersin

new.title: Eat künefe at Künefeci İsmail Usta
new.desc: Künefe is a hot cheese-and-kadayıf dessert soaked in syrup and eaten straight from the pan. Künefeci İsmail Usta on Silifke Caddesi is known for balanced syrup and good Hatay cheese.
new.tip: Closes around 20:00; eat it hot with Turkish tea.
new.q: Künefeci İsmail Usta, Çankaya, Silifke Cd., Akdeniz, Mersin

new.title: Start the day with tarmer soup at Tarsuslu Murat Usta
new.desc: Tarmer is a Tarsus-style breakfast soup finished with tahini sauce, served early in the morning and rare outside the province. Tarsuslu Murat Usta in Kiremithane is a classic morning stop.
new.tip: Go early before 10:00; it can sell out.
new.q: Tarsuslu Murat Usta, Kiremithane, Akdeniz, Mersin

new.title: Eat şireli börek at Yürü Börek & Künefe
new.desc: Şireli börek is a syrup-soaked pastry of the Mersin region, eaten as a sweet breakfast. Yürü Börek on Silifke Caddesi is known for it and for its künefe.
new.tip: Pair with tea in the morning; the pastry is best fresh.
new.q: Yürü Börek & Künefe, Cumhuriyet, Silifke Cd., Yenişehir, Mersin

new.title: Taste levrekli içli köfte at Kiremithane
new.desc: Kiremithane restaurant in the Kültür district serves a Mersin meze table with batata harra and levrekli içli köfte, a fish-stuffed version of the bulgur dumpling. It is a popular mid-range place for local dinners.
new.tip: Order several mezes to share; reservations help at weekends.

new.title: Look into St Paul's Well in Tarsus
new.desc: The well in the courtyard of a house in central Tarsus is traditionally said to be on the site of St Paul's family home. The excavated Roman street and the church next to it are part of the heritage trail.
new.tip: Small entry fee; combine it with the Roman road and Cleopatra's Gate.

new.title: See Cleopatra's Gate in Tarsus
new.desc: Cleopatra's Gate, also called the Kancık Gate, is the only ancient city gate still standing in Tarsus, with a Roman-era arch heavily restored. By tradition Antony and Cleopatra passed through it when they met in 41 BC.
new.tip: Free and open at all times; view from the pavement, as it sits in busy traffic.

new.title: Browse Tarsus's Kırkkaşık Bedesteni
new.desc: The Kırkkaşık covered bazaar was built in 1579 and is the main Ottoman market building of Tarsus. Souvenirs, coffee and craftwork are sold under its vaults.
new.tip: Weekday mornings are busiest; Tarsusi coffee is served nearby.

new.title: Picnic at the Tarsus Waterfall on the Berdan
new.desc: The Berdan (Cydnus) river drops over cascades just north of Tarsus, and the riverside park around it is a favourite family picnic place. Cafés and tea gardens line the banks.
new.tip: Weekends are crowded; weekday evenings are calmer.

new.title: Visit Eshab-ı Kehf, the Seven Sleepers cave near Tarsus
new.desc: This cave and mosque complex on the hillside near Tarsus is one of the places said to be where the Seven Sleepers slept for centuries. It draws pilgrims throughout the year.
new.tip: Free to enter; dress modestly and avoid prayer times.

new.title: Climb Gözlükule, the Neolithic mound of Tarsus
new.desc: Gözlükule is a settlement mound where excavations led by Hetty Goldman in the 1930s found occupation from the Neolithic through to Islamic times. The hill sits in south-eastern Tarsus.
new.tip: Little interpretation on site; visit for the view and the layers visible in the cut.

new.title: Eat Tarsus çöreği at Havana Pasta Gofret
new.desc: Havana Pasta Gofret has been open on İsmetpaşa Bulvarı since 1950 and is known for Tarsus çöreği, a sesame-topped pastry. It also sells gofret wafers and cakes.
new.tip: Buy a bag of çörek to take home; mornings are best.
new.q: Havana Pasta Gofret, İsmetpaşa Bulvarı, İsmetpaşa, Tarsus, Mersin

new.title: Eat hand-mashed humus at Akın Humus in Tarsus
new.desc: Tarsus is known for its humus, here hand-mashed and finished with melted butter and red pepper. Akın Humus is a morning favourite in the old town.
new.tip: Go before noon; eat with fresh bread.

new.title: Eat kuşgözü lahmacun at Azim Baba in Tarsus
new.desc: Azim Baba on Adana Bulvarı bakes kuşgözü lahmacun, a small bird's-eye-sized version, in a wood oven. It is a Tarsus speciality.
new.tip: Order several; they arrive in stacks.
new.q: Azim Baba Restaurant, Adana Bulvarı No:22, Şehitkerim, Tarsus, Mersin

new.title: Climb Silifke Castle above the Göksu
new.desc: Silifke Castle crowns a rocky hill over the town; King Leo granted it to the Hospitallers in 1210, and most of the present oval fortress dates to the Crusader period. About ten of the 23 towers Evliya Çelebi counted survive, around a dry moat and a large cistern.
new.tip: Small fee; go early or late for the light and the view over the Göksu valley.

new.title: Cross the Roman Taşköprü bridge in Silifke
new.desc: The Taşköprü is a Roman bridge built in AD 77-78 over the Göksu (Calycadnus) river in the centre of Silifke. It has been repaired many times but still carries traffic.
new.tip: Free and always open; photograph it from the riverside promenade.

new.title: Find St Thecla's ruins at Aya Tekla
new.desc: Meryemlik, near Silifke, is a pilgrimage site of the early Christian saint Thecla, said to have lived in a cave here; the ruins of a large 5th-century basilica stand over the cave church. It was one of the major pilgrimage centres of the Mediterranean.
new.tip: Small fee; take water, there is little shade.
new.q: Aya Tekla Church, Meryemlik, Silifke, Mersin

new.title: Walk the ruins of Uzuncaburç (Diocaesarea)
new.desc: Uzuncaburç, ancient Olba and later Diocaesarea, stands in the hills north of Silifke around the Temple of Zeus Olbios from the 3rd century BC and a tall Hellenistic tower. A colonnaded street, theatre and nymphaeum survive.
new.tip: Allow 2-3 hours and start in the morning; village stalls sell pomegranate juice.

new.title: Spot birds on the Göksu Delta
new.desc: The Göksu Delta is a Ramsar wetland of lagoons, reedbeds and dunes where flamingos, herons and the purple swamphen can be seen. Akgöl lake and the sea-turtle nesting beach are the main draws.
new.tip: Go in spring or autumn for migration; a morning visit is best.

new.title: Take a day boat from Taşucu harbour
new.desc: Taşucu is the ferry port for northern Cyprus and also the start of day yacht tours along the coast toward Kızkalesi and the Göksu delta. The harbour has fish restaurants and an amphora museum.
new.tip: Tours run in summer; confirm departures at the harbour.

new.title: See Cilician amphorae at the Taşucu Aslan Eyce museum
new.desc: The Aslan Eyce Taşucu Amphora Museum shows amphorae from the ancient wine and oil trade that passed through the Cilician coast. It is a small but focused collection near the harbour.
new.tip: Quick visit of 30-45 minutes; closed Mondays.
new.q: Aslan Eyce Taşucu Amfora Müzesi, Taşucu, Silifke, Mersin

new.title: See the Three Graces mosaic at Narlıkuyu
new.desc: A 4th-century Roman bath at Narlıkuyu is floored with a mosaic of the Three Graces, now protected as a small museum. The village has a harbour with fish restaurants.
new.tip: Tiny museum; pair with Cennet and Cehennem a few km north.
new.q: Narlıkuyu Mozaik Müzesi, Narlıkuyu, Silifke, Mersin

new.title: Eat lokma at Öğretmenin Yeri in Narlıkuyu
new.desc: Narlıkuyu Lokmacısı Öğretmenin Yeri is a small lokma shop in Narlıkuyu, known for syrup-soaked fried dough. It is a snack stop between the cave sites and the sea.
new.tip: Eat the lokma hot with tea.
new.q: Narlıkuyu Lokmacısı Öğretmenin Yeri, Çerkez Sokak No:8A, Narlıkuyu, Silifke, Mersin

new.title: Descend into Cennet, the Heaven sinkhole
new.desc: Cennet is a 70 m deep sinkhole with the ruins of a 5th-century chapel to the Virgin Mary at its base, reached by a staircase of about 450 steps. Next to it Cehennem (Hell), 128 m deep, is where Zeus kept Typhon in myth.
new.tip: Wear sturdy shoes; the staircase takes about 30 minutes each way, and an elevator has operated since 2020.
new.q: Cennet Çukuru, Cennet ve Cehennem Mağaraları, Silifke, Mersin

new.title: Visit Astım Cave, a lit stalactite cave
new.desc: Astım (Asthma) Cave is a lit cavern with stalactites and stalagmites, close to Cennet-Cehennem. Its humid air is said to ease breathing.
new.tip: Combine with Cennet-Cehennem; cool inside year round.

new.title: See the sea castle from Kızkalesi beach
new.desc: Kızkalesi, the Maiden's Castle, stands on a small island about 200 m offshore, rebuilt by the Armenians of Cilicia on earlier Byzantine foundations and once linked by a causeway to the mainland castle. Swimmers can paddle out in summer.
new.tip: Best seen from the beach at sunset; pensions along the front serve food.

new.title: Explore the land castle at Korykos
new.desc: Korykos is the mainland castle opposite the sea castle, begun by Byzantines and extended under the Armenian kings of Cilicia. A double wall with towers and a moat encloses its courtyard and a small chapel.
new.tip: Small fee; go early; swimming beaches are right outside.

new.title: Look into the Kanlıdivane sinkhole
new.desc: Kanlıdivane, ancient Canytelis, is built around a sinkhole about 130 m long and 70 m deep. Ruins include rock tombs, a tower inscribed by a priest-king of Olba and Byzantine basilicas.
new.tip: Small fee; the Mersin Music Festival sometimes stages concerts here.

new.title: Walk Elaiussa Sebaste by the sea at Ayaş
new.desc: Elaiussa Sebaste was a Roman and Byzantine port city on a peninsula at Ayaş with a theatre, baths, a colonnaded street, a necropolis and mosaics. Excavations continue every summer.
new.tip: Free site open by day; combine with a swim at Ayaş beach.
new.q: Elaiussa Sebaste Antik Kenti, Ayaş, Erdemli, Mersin

new.title: Pick your fish at Çakıl Balık in Ayaş
new.desc: Çakıl Balık Restaurant stands on Atatürk Caddesi in Ayaş, on the coast road west of Erdemli near the Elaiussa Sebaste ruins. Diners choose the fish and how it is cooked, with sea views from the tables.
new.tip: Pair it with a visit to the nearby Elaiussa Sebaste ruins.
new.q: Çakıl Balık Restaurant, Atatürk Caddesi, Ayaş, Erdemli, Mersin

new.title: Climb to Alahan Monastery above Mut
new.desc: Alahan Monastery is an early Christian complex built in two phases in the mid-5th century under Leo I and later under Zeno, with basilicas, a baptistery and a carved portal. It sits above Geçimli village in the Isauria hills.
new.tip: Open daily; dress for wind and bring water.

new.title: Explore Mut Castle
new.desc: Mut Castle is a Karamanid-era fortress on a hill above the town of Mut, with views over the Göksu valley. The Lal Ağa mosque and Ulu Cami are nearby.
new.tip: Free to walk up; take water in summer.

new.title: See Mamure Castle by the Anamur coast
new.desc: Mamure Castle is a huge coastal fortress built by the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia; Seljuk sultan Alaattin Keykubat enlarged it in 1221 and the Ottomans annexed it in 1469.
new.tip: Open daily with a small fee; go late afternoon.

new.title: Walk the ghost city of Anemurium
new.desc: Anemurium lies near Anamur at the southernmost tip of Anatolia and has three large baths, a necropolis of about 350 tombs, a theatre and an odeon. It was sacked by the Sasanians in 260 and abandoned by the 7th century.
new.tip: Take water and an hour for the baths and necropolis.

new.title: Visit Aynalıgöl cave in Aydıncık
new.desc: Aynalıgöl, also known as Gilindire Cave, is a cave in Aydıncık with a lake inside and stalactites. It lies close to the coast.
new.tip: Humid cave; wear non-slip shoes.

new.title: Hike the Cehennem Deresi canyon at Çamlıyayla
new.desc: Cehennem Deresi (Hell Creek) is a rocky gorge near Çamlıyayla in the Taurus, popular for walks and picnics. Namrun Castle also lies in the district.
new.tip: Go from late spring to autumn.

new.title: Stand at Gülek Castle on the Cilician Gates
new.desc: Gülek Castle is a medieval fortress near the Gülek Pass in the Taurus, controlling the historic road between Anatolia and Cilicia. Armenian and Ottoman building phases are visible.
new.tip: Roadside access; drive up for the view.

new.title: Tour a banana grove at Bozyazı
new.desc: Bozyazı is one of the few places in Turkey where bananas grow in greenhouses and outdoors; the town also makes banana-fibre handicrafts.
new.tip: Visit in autumn when the fruit is ripe.
